title: Delicate bubble of expelled material around the cool red star U Antliae
caption: The shell around the cool red star U Antliae, imaged by ALMA

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This ALMA image shows a delicate shell of material around the cool red star U Antliae, in finer detail than has ever been possible before.

The shell records a brief, violent episode in the star's life. Some 2700 years ago, the star briefly lost mass very rapidly. In a period lasting only a few hundred years, it threw off, at high speed, the material that now makes up the shell.

Looking at the shell more closely reveals some evidence of thin, wispy clouds within it, known as filamentary substructures. Studying fine features like these helps astronomers understand how stars like U Antliae shed their material into space. ALMA can do this because it observes at millimetre wavelengths, which pick up cool gas that does not glow in visible light.

understand.summary: This image was made with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) in its Band 6, at a wavelength of about 1.3 millimetres. The colour mapping is not published.
filters: 1.3 mm · Millimeter 230 GHz (Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Band 6)
understand.eye: Millimetre-wave light is invisible to the eye, so this view of the shell cannot be seen directly.

alt: A thin, delicate shell of material surrounding a star.
